semis.why: Day after a +4.3% SOX session (5th straight, 5d +12.5%, median +11.4% over 50d, AMD rsi73 / INTC rsi71) with the sector's own volume only 1.02x normal outside the two leaders; Asia proxies sold into their close (Hynix -1.45%, TSMC TW -0.6%) after the KOSPI failed to hold a 2% gap; pre-market -0.5% led by AMD -1.2 / AXTI -3.6 with no scheduled catalyst before the Xi visit (Sep 23-25) and Meta Connect (Sep 23). Beyond the gap: the Asia intraday reversal says the follow-through buyer is spent.

ai_power_infra.why: Scored on SOXX, so it inherits the semis give-back; the group itself is not stretched (median -1.1% vs 50d, pre +0.5%) so hold, not trim.

big_tech.why: Rotation, not exit: pre-market bid is in the UN-stretched megacaps (MSFT +0.8, GOOG +0.7, AMZN +0.5, all within 8% of the 50d) while META (-0.65 pre, rsi78) holds most of its +11% into Connect tomorrow; QQQ volume 1.42x on Monday = conviction. Beyond the +0.08% gap: the breadth of the bid inside big tech vs the fade inside chips.

sg_banks.why: STI +0.98% today on bank leadership with UOB on 2.16x volume, DBS 1.33x (conviction at the SGX close); banks +3-5% over 50d, rsi ~60 = not stretched; Xi state visit from tomorrow is a China-sentiment tailwind for SG; ~21h horizon.

market.why: Best S&P day since August is behind us; futures flat, 10Y eased 2bp to 4.94%, VIX 14.7 in contango; chip give-back offset by megacap rotation and summit optimism; Brent's overnight rebound above $102 caps the upside. Pre-summit, no-catalyst session = digestion.

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and don't add to chips today. Monday's blow-off in AMD, Intel and Meta is being digested, not extended, and the money is rotating into the less-stretched big tech names ahead of Xi's visit and Meta Connect tomorrow.
summary.where_we_are: 19:45 SGT, 07:45 ET, Tuesday Sep 22. US pre-market, 1h45m to the open; SGX closed (+0.98%). No major US print today: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson speaks at 22:20 SGT, the weekly ADP employment figure lands at 01:15 SGT. Xi Jinping's state visit runs Sep 23-25 and Meta Connect is Sep 23.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil moved most since the last US close: Brent fell more than 3% on Monday and then rebounded nearly 2% in Asia to above $102 on the Bessent Iranian-airline headline (Investing.com, Sep 22), while the 10-year eased 2 bp to 4.94%, the dollar and VIX (14.7) are flat and today's calendar is minor. The leans do not depend on oil; it is a cap on the whole market, not the reason for the chip call.
what_happened: Chip stocks rallied 4.3% on Monday, the fifth straight gain, with AMD +10% to a $1 trillion valuation, Intel +12% and Meta +11% after its Muse AI agent topped the App Store (Bloomberg, Sep 21; CNBC, Sep 22). The chip index is now 12.5% higher in five sessions and the median chip name sits 11% above its 50-day line (tape).

The conviction was in the leaders, not the sector: AMD traded 1.9x and Intel 1.7x normal volume, but the median chip name only 1.0x (tape, Mon close). AMD's RSI is 73 and Intel's 71; Meta's is 78. That is a stretched tape by any price-feed measure.

Asia could not hold the follow-through: the KOSPI opened up 2% and closed +0.3%, Taiwan erased a 1.5% gain to close +0.2%, and the two Asian chip proxies closed down, SK Hynix -1.45% and TSMC Taiwan -0.6% (Investing.com, Sep 22; tape). Chips are -0.5% pre-market with AMD -1.2% and AXT -3.6% (tape, thin).

Big tech is bid where it is not stretched: Microsoft +0.8%, Google +0.7% and Amazon +0.5% pre-market, all within 8% of their 50-day, while Meta gives back 0.65% (tape). S&P futures are flat, the 10-year is 4.94% and the VIX is 14.7 with the curve calm (tape).

Singapore banks led the STI +0.98% to 5,728 today with UOB on 2.2x normal volume and DBS on 1.3x (tape, SGX close). Investors are holding expectations low for the Trump-Xi meeting to break new ground (Reuters via Investing.com, Sep 22).

per_group.semis: Slightly down. The day after a 4.3% index surge with the leaders at RSI 70+ and only normal sector volume, the Asian chip proxies sold into their close, and there is no scheduled catalyst before Xi and Connect tomorrow; that reversal is what the read adds beyond the thin -0.5% pre-market print.
per_group.ai_power_infra: Slightly down on its chip benchmark. The group itself is not stretched (median 1% below its 50-day, Infineon and Bloom up pre-market), so hold rather than trim.
per_group.big_tech: Slightly up. Money is rotating into the un-stretched megacaps, Microsoft, Google and Amazon, while Meta holds most of its 11% gain into Connect; Monday's 1.4x Nasdaq volume says the bid is real.
per_group.sg_banks: Slightly up at Wednesday's SGX close. Heavy-volume bank buying into today's close and a calm US tape, with Xi's visit a China-sentiment tailwind; the banks are only 3-5% over their 50-day.
per_group.market: Flat. Monday was the S&P's best day since August; the chip give-back is offset by the megacap rotation and summit optimism, and the oil rebound caps the upside.

change_my_mind: AMD and Intel both hold Monday's close through the first hour: the fade is wrong, chips flip to slightly up.
Chip index volume above 1.2x its 10-day average on a green tape: buyers are not exhausted, chips flip to slightly up.
10-year above 4.98% or VIX above 16: this is a macro sell, not digestion, and big tech goes slightly down too.
Any agency action on chip export controls around the Xi visit before the close moves chips harder than anything on this tape, in either direction.
summary.confidence: the chip call fades a five-day momentum run that this record has lost on three times running, the Asian reversal is the only new evidence, and pre-market prints have no volume behind them.
summary.cant_know: Whether Monday's chasers sell today or wait for Connect and Xi; same-day sector direction after a blow-off is close to a coin flip and the Asian fade is the one tilt.
summary.the_call: Chips slightly down, moderate, around 0.5-1.5%, with AMD, Intel and the small substrate names giving back the most. Big tech slightly up on Microsoft, Google and Amazon while Meta pauses. The broad market flat. Singapore banks slightly up at tomorrow's close.
